title: POC post-brief: business case + rollout proposal
body:
Executive summary:

This document captures the post-POC readout for the ACME Corp generative search proof-of-concept (completed 2025-02-12). The POC validated that Redwood Inference can meet ACME's latency and throughput targets for interactive search augmentation while reducing per-query cost compared to their incumbent cloud-hosted LLM endpoints. The goal of this brief is to (1) summarize technical findings and business impact, (2) present a recommended phased rollout with cost and risk tradeoffs, and (3) surface the next commercial and engineering asks required to transition from POC to production.

POC scope and success criteria (restated):
- Scope: Integrate Redwood hosted/runtime with ACME's search frontend and vector store, evaluate answer relevance, latency (p95 target <= 450ms external), throughput (sustained 200 qps), cost per 1k queries, and deployment options (hosted vs dedicated).
- Success criteria:
  - Relevance: >12% improvement in NDCG@10 on the evaluation set vs baseline (ACME's current reranking).
  - Latency: p95 <= 450ms for short queries; p50 <= 140ms.
  - Cost: <= 0.75x current per-query spend at expected traffic volumes using batching + KV prefix caching.
  - Reliability: <1% error rate during a 48-hour soak test.

High-level outcomes vs criteria: 
- Relevance: Achieved +14% NDCG@10 using mix of response prompting and a small retrieval-augmented model variant. Quality regressions were minimal on slot-heavy queries; a small template adjustment improved stability.
- Latency: p95 observed at 410ms when using a dedicated small-gpu pool with continuous batching and prefix cache; hosted baseline (multi-tenant) saw p95 of ~540ms under burst traffic.
- Cost: Estimated per-query unit cost reduced to ~0.68x of ACME's incumbent when using continuous batching + 8-bit quantized model variant on dedicated capacity. Hosted mode without commit-level discounts came in at ~1.05x.
- Reliability: Error rate 0.6% during soak; root causes were transient network spikes and an edge case in request size handling that we patched.

Key technical findings (concise):
- Batching profiles: Continuous batching produced the largest unit-cost wins for short queries when traffic sustained >80 qps. Cold-starts for isolated spikes increased p95 in the hosted tier.
- Prefix caching: KV-caching of conversation prefixes reduced token generation volume by ~22% for repeat queries, disproportionately benefiting conversational flows.
- Model variants: A quantized 8-bit variant (same architecture) provided acceptable quality with 30-40% throughput improvement on the same GPU type; lower memory footprint enabled better consolidation for Dedicated pools.
- Tokenization anomalies: A small set of product names triggered tokenization mismatches causing subtle hallucinations; we added a pre-token filter as a mitigation.

Operational and business implications: 
- Recommended commercial entry: Start with a small Dedicated commitment (2x small GPU nodes) for the first 3 months to meet latency SLOs and prove cost targets. This unlocks the 20% price break compared to hosted list pricing and reduces p95 during bursts.
- SRE/Support: Need a 24/7 on-call rotation during the first 60 days of production to troubleshoot edge cases and collect realistic traffic profiles.
- Data governance: ACME requires VPC peering for private traffic lanes; security sign-off was conditional on enabling KMS for model call audit logs (we confirmed compatibility).

Recommended rollout options (tradeoffs):
1) Phased Dedicated (recommended)
   - Timeline: 6–10 weeks to provision, integrate, test canary -> full traffic.
   - Pros: Predictable latency, cost efficiency, easier quality repro. 
   - Cons: Lead time for GPU allocation; minimum commitment.
2) Hosted with burst routing to Dedicated
   - Timeline: 2–4 weeks for API integration + routing policy.
   - Pros: Fastest time-to-value; no min commit upfront.
   - Cons: Slightly higher unit cost; p95 during spikes may exceed target unless routing configured.
3) Hybrid on-prem gateway (long term)
   - Timeline: 12+ weeks; involves network & compliance audits.
   - Pros: Meets strict data residency/compliance; full control.
   - Cons: Heavy ops lift; higher TCO initially.

Detailed recommended next steps (practical, with owners):
- Commercial
  - SE/AE: Present Dedicated pricing sketch and commitment options to ACME procurement (Owner: Priya Nair) — due: 2025-02-27
  - Legal: Start SOC/Contract addendum review for VPC peering and KMS usage (Owner: Sofia Martinez) — due: 2025-03-07

- Engineering
  - Infra: Provision 2x small GPU nodes in customer-dedicated pool; enable KV caching and continuous batching (Owner: Liam O'Connor) — due: 2025-03-10
  - SDK/Integration: Patch pre-tokenization filter into client adapter and ship a 0.2.1 release for ACME integration testing (Owner: Ethan Cole) — due: 2025-02-28
  - SRE: Define alert runbook for p95 latency > 500ms and error rate >1% during canary (Owner: SRE lead, name TBD) — due: 2025-02-25

- Product & Ops
  - Product: Lock canary metrics dashboard for model-level latency, unit cost, and NDCG trends (Owner: Product-hosted-api) — due: 2025-03-03
  - Solutions Eng: Run a 2-hour workshop with ACME search team on prompt templates, tokenization quirks, and fallbacks (Owner: Priya Nair) — due: 2025-02-24

Risk register (top items):
- Capacity availability: GPU procurement lead time could push Dedicated rollout by 2–4 weeks (mitigation: temporary hosted burst routing).
- Edge-case hallucinations: Tokenization anomaly could surface on broader product names (mitigation: input sanitization and add targeted evals to the monitoring suite).
- Contract timing: Legal negotiation delays risk start of committed term; propose a short pilot contract that transitions to Dedicated upon signature.

KPIs to measure during canary (and thresholds):
- Latency: p95 <= 450ms (red > 550ms), p50 <= 140ms.
- Quality: NDCG@10 improvement >= 12% (red < 8%).
- Cost: per-query cost <= 0.80x incumbent (red > 0.95x).
- Reliability: error rate <1% (red >2%).

Decision points for ACME leadership meeting (recommended agenda items):
1) Accept Dedicated commitment: yes/no? (financial and timing parameters)
2) Approve SLOs and canary timelines
3) Sign off on data governance checklist (KMS + VPC peering)

Appendix (quick references & artifacts):
- Raw benchmark CSVs and plotting: https://s3.redwood.ai/poc/acme/benchmarks-20250212.csv
- Evaluation prompts/examples: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SE/ACME+POC+evals
- Shortlist of model variants and config used in tests: model-A-8q8 (quantized), model-A-fp16

Notes and open questions (working items):
- ACME product team requested a deterministic response mode for compliance logging — need to clarify acceptability and potential latency impact.
- Ask procurement whether a 3-month trial with a conversion credit is acceptable to accommodate contract lead time.

Summary recommendation (single line):
Move to a small Dedicated commitment for an 8-week canary, run the outlined engineering fixes and monitoring, and reconvene with ACME to convert to steady-state Dedicated or hybrid routing based on measured KPIs.

Document history (light):
- 2025-02-15: initial draft after POC closeout (Ethan Cole)
- 2025-02-18: added cost modeling and quantized variant numbers (Liam O'Connor)
- 2025-02-22: updated timeline after legal intake call (Priya Nair)
